classification.difficultyReason: Requires locating an unmarked circle centre from equal chords before applying Pythagoras.

content.prompt: Find the radius of the two circles that cover the square of side length $4\text{ cm}$, as depicted below.

spec.description: Two congruent overlapping circles cover a square. Their intersections are the midpoints of the square's top and bottom edges; each circle also passes through the two corners on its respective side. Complete circle outlines extend beyond the square.
spec.mathematics: Reconstruction coordinates: square [0,4] × [0,4], circle centres (1,2) and (3,2), equal radii sqrt(5). Coordinates and centres are construction data only and are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: No centres, radii, construction lines or answers appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
$\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}$.

Locate the centre using perpendicular bisectors, then apply Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
Consider the left circle. The square's left side and the segment joining the two circle intersections are parallel chords, each $4\text{ cm}$ long. Their perpendicular bisector is the horizontal line halfway up the square. The top-left corner and the upper circle intersection form another chord of length $2\text{ cm}$, so the centre lies $1\text{ cm}$ from the square's left side.

The radius to the top-left corner is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with legs $1\text{ cm}$ and $2\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}r^2&=1^2+2^2\\r^2&=5\\r&=\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

The other circle has the same radius.
